text:
alex: quick sketch — spike idea for 'sidecarless' tenant routing. instead of per-tenant sidecars we push a regional relay that preserves tenant identity at the application layer and avoids per-customer iptables. thinking: relay does authz by TLS + short-lived tenant tokens, and we keep per-tenant routing via header/ID. tradeoffs: source-ip preservation for legacy clients, egress cost, and blast radius.
priya: curious — how do you propose to prove tenant identity without mTLS from sidecar? that was the whole point of sidecars.
alex: two options: 1) keep mTLS between customer-hosted agents and relay (but lightweight TLS termination only) OR 2) embed a signed tenant-assertion token inside the initial TLS handshake via ALPN token exchange or via an in-band AUTH header after connection. option 2 reduces fleet of certs but relies on token issuance flow.
jamie: option 1 keeps source IPs and avoids NAT gymnastics. option 2 will require a NAT unless we route via static egress IPs per customer which we cannot afford at scale.
maria: security: tokens are fine but need short TTL + aud claim + rotation. also need to ensure replay protection — recommend mTLS or SPIFFE x509 when possible. tokens alone increase attacker surface if agent compromised.
dan: ops question — if we centralize relay, how do we handle degraded relay region? graceful failover? We can't route all to another region without increasing latency for some customers.
alex: plan in spike: prototype both: a) relay with mTLS + preserved src ip via proxy protocol, and b) relay without mTLS using signed tenant tokens and per-connection ephemeral NAT. measure: cost (NAT/gw), latency p50/p95, rollout complexity, cert management overhead. rollout path: start with a small cohort using mTLS-relay, then evaluate token path for customers that can't run sidecars.
priya: implementation note: envoy supports proxy_protocol and headers for tenant id. example config snippet to pass original addr:
```
listener:
  use_proxy_proto: true
  filter_chains: ...
```

jamie: +1 for realistic metrics. we should also simulate controlplane churn: cert rotation, token issuer outage, relay autoscale. those are common blowups.
maria: add audit logs requirement — every tenant assertion must be logged with correlation id. compliance will need retention window.
alex: ok i'll open a short spike ticket with acceptance criteria: perf budget (p95 < 200ms extra), cost delta < 15% for typical workload, migration playbook, and failure-mode doc. anyone want to join the spike pairing session tomorrow? :calendar:
priya: i'll join for the token flow tests.
dan: i'll help with chaos tests for relay failover.
infra-bot: deploy-notes: spike branch created: sidecarless-relay-spike. CI pipeline queued.
alex: thanks — i'll add a lightweight RFC followup once we have initial numbers and a recommended path. :thumbsup:
